topic: structuredClone vs JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()): the JSON round trip drops undefined, turns Map and Set into {}, and throws on cycles
text:
Deep copy or lossy copy?

JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj)) looks like a deep clone, but it quietly rewrites your data:

• undefined and functions in an object disappear
• NaN and Infinity become null
• a Date comes back as an ISO string
• Map and Set become {}
• a circular reference throws "TypeError: cyclic object value"

The fix is one line: structuredClone(obj). It's built in and has been available across browsers since March 2022. It keeps circular references. If something can't be cloned, like a function, it throws a DataCloneError instead of silently dropping it.

My rule of thumb: structuredClone for copying state, JSON only when you actually want JSON. Class instances still lose their methods, so clone plain data.

Which bug did a JSON deep copy cause in your codebase?
